name: NH Tech Alliance Innovation Summit
audience: technology executives, entrepreneurs, investors, legislators
description: New Hampshire's annual gathering of innovation leaders, featuring the Entrepreneur of the Year awards and a Startup Showcase where early-stage companies give five-minute pitches.

name: NH Tech Alliance Cybersecurity Summit
audience: IT leaders, security practitioners, business owners
description: A full-day summit on the cybersecurity threats facing New Hampshire businesses, mixing practitioner talks with hands-on tabletop incident-response exercises.

name: NH Tech Alliance Product of the Year
audience: entrepreneurs, investors, local business community
description: Now in its 20th year, five New Hampshire tech and advanced-manufacturing finalists demo their products live on stage; the winner is chosen 50% by audience vote and 50% by expert judges.

name: Speed Venture Summit
audience: early-stage founders, New England investors
description: Speed-dating for fundraising: early-stage New England startups rotate through 10-minute one-on-one meetings with regional investors. Run by the NH Tech Foundation.

name: eBrew
audience: creative and technical professionals on the NH Seacoast
description: A 25-year-old after-work networking series billed as New Hampshire's premier creative and technical Seacoast meetup; upcoming Portsmouth sessions are 20 October and 2 December 2026.

name: Meeting in the Millyard
audience: New Hampshire technology and advanced manufacturing community
description: Multi-day New Hampshire Tech Alliance flagship gathering, listed on the Alliance's official events calendar for 18-20 May 2027 in Nashua.

name: Northeast Dreamin'
audience: Salesforce admins, developers, consultants and users in the Northeast
description: The Northeast's community-run Salesforce user conference, with keynotes, multiple speaker tracks, a sponsor expo and a nonprofit track.

name: Business Value Builder Summit
venue: Dutch Miller Deck, Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Marshall University
audience: startup founders, small and mid-sized business owners, CEOs
description: Run by the Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (iCenter) at Marshall University, this half-day summit covers growth systems, company valuation, leadership teams and exit planning for West Virginia founders.

name: Silicon Couloir Pitch Day
audience: Wyoming entrepreneurs, investors, general public
description: Wyoming's longest-running startup pitch competition, in its fifteenth year: coached finalists pitch to judges and a live Jackson audience for cash prizes, with a public livestream. Free to attend.

name: PEI BioAlliance Summer Social
audience: PEI bioscience and life-science cluster companies and partners
description: The main summer networking event for Prince Edward Island's bioscience technology cluster, held on the Charlottetown waterfront and open to all cluster companies and partners.

name: PEI BioAlliance Holiday Social
audience: PEI bioscience sector companies and cluster partners
description: Free year-end networking reception for Prince Edward Island's bioscience cluster, open to all sector companies and partners in Charlottetown.

name: Vintage Computer Festival East
audience: retro-computing hobbyists, collectors, restorers, families
description: The East Coast's largest vintage computing festival: three days of exhibits, classes, talks, a repair workshop, consignment and vendors on the InfoAge museum campus.

name: Vintage Computer Festival West
audience: retro-computing enthusiasts, collectors, computer historians
description: Two days of vintage hardware exhibits, speaker talks and the VCF After Dark social, hosted at the Computer History Museum in Silicon Valley.

name: Vintage Computer Festival Midwest
audience: retro-computing hobbyists, collectors, makers
description: A free two-day celebration of computer history run by Chicago Classic Computing: exhibitor tables, talks, an auction and a large buy/sell/trade marketplace for vintage kit.

name: Vintage Computer Festival Southeast
venue: Renaissance Atlanta Waverly Hotel & Convention Center
audience: retro-computing and retro-gaming enthusiasts
description: Machines from the 1960s through the 1990s on display, plus history talks, soldering sessions, consignment and vendors, co-located with the Southern Fried Gaming Expo.

name: Vintage Computer Festival Southwest
venue: The Westin Dallas Fort Worth Airport
audience: retro-computing collectors, restorers, students, families
description: Volunteer-run North Texas vintage computing show with 100+ exhibits and vendors, hands-on workshops, talks, a scholarship auction and a consignment shop. Youth under 17 free with an adult.

name: Vintage Computer Festival Montreal
audience: retro-computing enthusiasts and collectors in Quebec
description: Canada's Vintage Computer Federation event: a two-day weekend of vintage machine exhibits and talks in Montreal.

name: VCF Swap Meet
venue: Brookdale Wall Campus Parking, 6th Street and Monmouth Boulevard
audience: vintage computer, radio and electronics collectors
description: Twice-yearly outdoor tailgate marketplace for vintage computers, electronics, radios, TVs and ham gear. Five dollars admission, vendor spaces twenty-five. The following meet is 22 May 2027.

name: Portland Retro Gaming Expo
audience: retro gamers, collectors, gaming historians, families
description: Long-running classic video game convention with a free-play arcade, panels, industry guests and a large vendor hall; running annually since 2009.

name: SC Conference (Supercomputing)
audience: HPC researchers, system engineers, academics, national labs, vendors
description: The world's flagship high performance computing conference: technical papers, a very large exhibit floor, student cluster competitions and the SCinet research network built on site each year.

name: NICAR Conference
audience: data journalists, newsroom developers, educators, students
description: IRE's annual data journalism conference: hands-on classes from spreadsheet basics through R, Python and AI, plus newsroom tooling talks and receptions. IRE membership required to attend.

name: Code4Lib
audience: developers and technologists in libraries, museums and archives
description: The conference for people who code for libraries: an annual, community-organised gathering of technologists from libraries, museums and archives, running since 2006.

name: Dayton Hamvention
audience: amateur radio operators, electronics hobbyists, makers, students
description: The world's largest amateur radio gathering, marking its 75th year: vendor exhibits, a vast electronics flea market, D-STAR and DMR digital radio demos, license exams and technical forums. Students free.

name: Day of Data Detroit
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: A free one-day community event in the SQL Saturday tradition for database professionals and anyone working with data on any platform.

name: Salt Lake City Day of Data
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Free community day of sessions for database and data professionals, part of the long-running SQL Saturday network.

name: Day of Data Winnipeg
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Manitoba's free SQL Saturday format community day for database and data professionals working on any platform.

name: Day of Data Toronto
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Toronto's free community day of data sessions, run in the SQL Saturday tradition for database professionals and data practitioners.

name: Boston Data and AI Saturday
audience: database professionals, data engineers, AI practitioners
description: Boston's free SQL Saturday lineage community event, now broadened to cover data platform and AI topics.

name: Day of Data Pittsburgh
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Free one-day Pittsburgh community conference for data professionals, part of the SQL Saturday network.

name: Day of Data Orlando
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Orlando's free community day of data platform sessions in the SQL Saturday format.

name: Day of Data St Louis
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Free St. Louis community event for database and data professionals across any platform.

name: Houston Day of Data
audience: database professionals, data engineers, analysts
description: Houston's free SQL Saturday format community day covering the Microsoft data platform and broader data work.

name: MidCamp
audience: Drupal developers, designers, strategists, content and marketing people
description: The Midwest's Drupal camp: a day of sessions and training, a day of sessions plus an open-space unconference, and a contribution day, with 30+ sessions and a hackathon.

name: New England Drupal Camp
audience: Drupal users of all levels, from beginners to professionals
description: Volunteer-run, attendee-driven Drupal camp founded in 2014 to grow Drupal skills across New England, with training days and sessions for rookies and pros alike.

name: Florida DrupalCamp
audience: Drupal developers, site builders, UX strategists, open-source contributors
description: Three days in Orlando: Drupal training workshops, a day of technical sessions, and a contribution day, drawing 150+ attendees from around the world.

name: DrupalCon North America
audience: Drupal developers, agency leaders, content strategists, marketers, executives
description: The flagship North American Drupal conference, in Orlando for 2027, spanning developer sessions, agency and executive tracks, and community contribution days.

name: Southwestern Ontario Drupal Camp
audience: Drupal developers and site builders in southwestern Ontario
description: Regional Drupal camp for the southwestern Ontario community, listed on the official Drupal community events calendar for 23-24 October 2026.

name: Nashville Microsoft Community Day
audience: administrators, end users, architects and developers working with Microsoft 365
description: In its eleventh year, a free-to-low-cost community day of beginner through advanced sessions on Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Power Platform and related cloud services.

name: Vancouver Microsoft 365 Summit
audience: CIOs, IT architects, Microsoft MVPs and partners in Western Canada
description: Full-day Microsoft ecosystem summit with four tracks covering security and cloud infrastructure, modern workplace and AI, business applications, and innovation platforms, plus a speaker breakfast the next morning.

name: Texas Dreamin'
audience: Salesforce users, admins, developers and partners
description: Community-led two-day Salesforce conference organised by Texas user-group leaders, with keynotes, multiple session tracks and a strong career-building emphasis.

name: Cactusforce
audience: Salesforce developers, architects and advanced admins
description: More code, less fluff: a deeply technical community conference for Salesforce developers and architects, built around live demos, Q&A and Certified Technical Architect preparation rather than slideware.

name: Forcelandia
audience: Salesforce developers and the Portland Salesforce community
description: Portland's developer-oriented Salesforce community event, tagline Keeping Code Weird: a two-day, community-run gathering focused on technical content.

name: WordCamp New York City
audience: WordPress developers, designers, publishers, agency owners
description: New York City's community-organised WordPress conference, listed on WordCamp Central as in planning: talks, workshops and a contributor day for the local WordPress community.

name: WordCamp Santa Clarita
audience: WordPress developers, designers, bloggers, small business owners
description: Community-run WordPress camp for the Santa Clarita Valley and greater Los Angeles area, in planning for 2027 per WordCamp Central.

name: Chi Hack Night
venue: Hybrid, in person in Chicago plus YouTube livestream
audience: designers, researchers, data journalists, activists, policy people, developers
description: A free weekly Tuesday-evening civic tech hack night, 7 to 10pm, where Chicagoans build, share and learn about using data, design and technology to improve the city. No coding required.

name: Code for Boston Hack Night
audience: civic technologists, analysts, designers, government and nonprofit staff, residents
description: Free Tuesday-evening civic tech hack night: online weekly from 7pm and in person at the CIC on the first and third Tuesday of each month, working on software projects for the Boston area.

name: Ignite Seattle
audience: technologists, makers, storytellers and the general public
description: The original Ignite lightning-talk night: twelve speakers, five minutes each, twenty slides that auto-advance every fifteen seconds. Tickets twelve dollars early bird, twenty regular.

name: Circuit Hacking Monday at Noisebridge
audience: electronics beginners, hardware hackers, makers of all ages
description: Free weekly Monday 7pm electronics and soldering night at the Noisebridge hackerspace, no membership or payment required. Noisebridge also runs Gamebridge, a robotics meetup and the Five Minutes of Fame lightning-talk night.

name: North Forge FabLab Open House
venue: North Forge Fabrication Lab, 312 William Ave
audience: makers, hardware founders, students, curious members of the public
description: Free Tuesday 6pm guided tour of Manitoba's largest fabrication lab covering 3D printing, laser cutting, CNC routing and vacuum forming, showing how local entrepreneurs prototype hardware. Registration required.

name: Tech Titans Awards Gala
audience: North Texas technology executives, innovators, investors, academics
description: The 26th annual North Texas technology awards night, honouring innovators, corporate leaders and universities across several award tracks. Tech Titans also runs AI, cybersecurity and quantum forums and a startup summit.

name: Kentucky Entrepreneur Hall of Fame Induction Celebration
venue: Central Bank Center, 430 W Vine St
audience: Kentucky founders, investors, business and tech community
description: Annual dinner inducting Kentucky's leading entrepreneurs into the state Hall of Fame; one of the largest founder networking nights in the Bluegrass, listed on the Awesome Inc community calendar.

name: Awesome Fellowship Demo Day
audience: startup founders, investors, Kentucky tech community
description: Cohort demo day for the Awesome Fellowship startup accelerator in Lexington, powered by Chase, where fellows present their companies over lunch to the local ecosystem.

name: LaunchVT Demo Night
audience: Vermont founders, investors, community members
description: The public finale of LaunchVT, Vermont's free twelve-week spring accelerator: six to eight cohort companies pitch at Hula in Burlington for twenty thousand dollars of non-dilutive capital, in front of hundreds of community members.

name: The Idea Village Demo Day
audience: New Orleans founders, investors, ecosystem partners
description: Cohort demo day for The Idea Village's New Orleans accelerator programmes, where portfolio founders present to the city's investor and startup community.

name: 3rd Coast Venture Summit
audience: seed to Series A founders and investors across the Gulf South
description: The Idea Village's investor summit connecting Gulf South founders from Texas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama and Florida with national seed and Series A investors, via on-stage pitches, investor roundtables and app-matched one-to-one meetings.

name: Cultivate Conference
audience: growers, agtech startups, researchers, investors, policymakers
description: Grand Farm's flagship agtech conference, built around its Regional Agriculture Pain Point Report: panels, startup pitches and breakout workshops on herbicide resistance, pest management and farm labour shortages.

name: Elevate Conference
audience: ag industry leaders, startups, investors, researchers, growers
description: A one-day summit on applying AI to real farm work, covering predictive analytics, automation, sensing and computer vision, closing with a public Field Day of farm tours at the Grand Farm campus outside Fargo.

name: Autonomous Nation
audience: policymakers, robotics and autonomy engineers, startups, growers
description: Morning sessions on autonomy policy, deployment barriers and workforce readiness, followed by live afternoon field demonstrations of autonomous agricultural equipment.

name: StartupBREW Fargo
audience: entrepreneurs, innovators, creatives, community members
description: Emerging Prairie's weekly Wednesday-morning coffee meetup from 8 to 9:30am: thirty minutes of Coffee Club mingling, then a short speaker slot and a twenty-minute Q&A that deliberately favours dialogue over presentation.

name: Prairie Capital Summit
audience: founders, investors, students, SBDC advisors and financial professionals
description: Emerging Prairie's regional capital summit: keynotes, panels and breakouts on strengthening deal flow and closing the capital-access gap for Northern Plains entrepreneurs.

name: Founders Retreat
audience: company founders only
description: A three-day founders-only retreat run by Emerging Prairie in the Sheyenne River Valley: no pitches or panels, just facilitated small-group conversation, shared meals and rest, on pay-what-suits-you Chip In pricing.

name: DakotaCon
audience: security professionals, Dakota State University students, hobbyists
description: South Dakota's deliberately small security conference: two tracks of free Friday talks where you can actually reach the speakers, followed by the weekend-long Dakota Conquest capture-the-flag competition.

name: Build48
audience: aspiring founders, side-project builders, students
description: Genesis Centre's 48-hour zero-to-launched-product sprint in St. John's, covering problem framing, user validation, MVP build with AI tools, go-to-market and investment basics, with meals, mentors and AI credits. The 2026 edition sold out.

name: iFiveK
audience: Charleston tech professionals and their families
description: Charleston's tech community 5K and after-party, run since 2007 by the Charleston Digital Corridor: an evening race downtown followed by a large social, with proceeds funding Charleston Learning Center scholarships.

name: Charleston Digital Connect
audience: Charleston technology professionals, founders, job seekers
description: Charleston Digital Corridor's recurring morning networking session at the Charleston Tech Center, running alongside its AI Academy classes and SBDC workshops.

name: Mississippi Aerospace & Defense Symposium
audience: aerospace and defense industry, engineers, suppliers, policymakers
description: Three days of panels, keynotes and facility tours bringing together Mississippi's aerospace and defense technology leaders, listed on the Innovate Mississippi events calendar.

name: CONNECT: Networking for Entrepreneurs
audience: Mississippi entrepreneurs, mentors, investors
description: Innovate Mississippi's first-Thursday monthly networking evening from 4:30 to 6:30pm for entrepreneurs, mentors and investors, held at a Jackson brewery.

name: Agile Open Northwest
audience: agile practitioners, coaches, software developers and engineering managers
description: A two-day Open Space unconference with no pre-set programme: attendees propose and run every session themselves on the morning of day one. A long-running Pacific Northwest agile community event.

name: Global Game Jam - NYU Game Center
audience: game developers, artists, students, first-time jammers
description: NYU's Global Game Jam site: a 48-hour weekend where teams design and build a game to a surprise worldwide theme.

name: Global Game Jam - Parsons School of Design
venue: Parsons School of Design, Design and Technology
audience: game developers, designers, artists, students
description: The Parsons Design and Technology Global Game Jam site in Manhattan, running the international 48-hour jam weekend.

name: Global Game Jam - RPI Game Development Club
audience: students, hobbyist and professional game developers
description: The RPI Game Development Club's Global Game Jam site in Troy, New York: a 48-hour team build to the global theme.

name: Global Game Jam - Abilene Christian University
audience: students and local game developers in West Texas
description: West Texas's Global Game Jam site at Abilene Christian University, joining the worldwide 48-hour game-making weekend.

name: Global Game Jam - AAPI in Gaming
audience: game developers, artists and writers, with a focus on the AAPI community
description: Vancouver's AAPI in Gaming Global Game Jam site, running the international 48-hour jam with a focus on welcoming Asian American and Pacific Islander creators.
